sources.title: Albert Schwarz and Oleg Zaboronsky, Supersymmetry and localization
sources.locator: Complete 16-page paper retrieved. Section 2, PDF pp. 2–3, on ΠTM, odd vector fields, and the invariant Berezin volume; Section 3, PDF pp. 4–7, Theorem 1 statement and complete proof, including div(dV)Q=0, compactness, Q-squared conditions, and vanishing integrals of Q-exact terms.

contents.name: Section 2: finite-dimensional odd tangent bundle and Berezin integration
contents.support: The paper identifies functions on ΠTM with differential forms, gives the odd vector field Q and its square, and states the divergence-free condition for the canonical Berezin volume. The local definition fixes the integral, grading, Q-invariance identity, and boundary condition explicitly.

contents.name: Section 3, Theorem 1 and proof: localization of a finite-dimensional supermanifold integral
contents.support: The source proves a distinct fixed-locus localization theorem under compactness, div(dV)Q=0, and compactness of Q², using Q-invariant localization functions and the vanishing of integrals of Q-exact terms. These conventions and the boundary requirement inform the formulation; the finite-parameter derivative and constancy proof in this item is local and does not import the source's stronger theorem.

sources.title: Vasily Pestun and Maxim Zabzine, Introduction to localization in quantum field theory
sources.locator: Complete 19-page chapter retrieved. Section 1, PDF pp. 1–3: ΠTM formulation, the Q-exact finite-dimensional deformation, Stokes-based t-independence for δ²W=0, the subsequent saddle limit, and the caveat that infinite-dimensional extensions require all formal steps to be defined.

contents.name: Section 1: finite-dimensional Q-exact deformation and separate large-parameter limit
contents.support: The chapter presents a compact-manifold ΠTM integral and its Q-exact deformation, then distinguishes t-independence from the additional t→∞ saddle evaluation. The local theorem states explicit derivative majorants and zero-boundary hypotheses and asserts no saddle limit.

contents.name: Section 1: limitations of the infinite-dimensional extension
contents.support: The authors state that a formal infinite-dimensional extension requires the finite-dimensional formal properties and determinant operations to be defined. The definition and theorem are explicitly restricted to finite-dimensional data.

sources.title: Gerald B. Folland, Real Analysis, 2nd ed.
sources.locator: Complete book text retrieved. Chapter 2, §2.27, printed pp. 55–56: parts (a)–(b), with the full sequential dominated-convergence proof for differentiation under the integral sign and the note that the estimate may be taken on a compact subinterval of an open parameter interval.

contents.name: Theorem 2.27(b): differentiation under the integral sign
contents.support: The theorem requires integrable sections and one L1 majorant for the parameter derivative uniformly on the parameter interval; its proof uses the mean-value theorem and dominated convergence. The local proof applies it on open neighborhoods contained in each compact parameter interval, matching the imported supplier's exact hypotheses.

contents.name: Theorem 2.27 and proof: real-analysis support for the exact differentiation supplier
contents.support: The cited book is a full textbook treatment of Lebesgue integration and supplies the analytic convention for the parameterized integral. The authored definition records the precise L1-majorant conditions instead of relying on the citation as proof.

sources.title: Jiří Lebl, Basic Analysis I
sources.locator: Complete relevant HTML section inspected. Section 4.2.4, Proposition 4.2.6 and proof, lines 725–738: zero derivative on an interval implies constancy by applying the mean value theorem on the segment between arbitrary points.

contents.name: Section 4.2.4, Proposition 4.2.6: zero derivative implies constancy
contents.support: The source gives the exact real-valued zero-derivative corollary used after taking real and imaginary parts. The local proof also retains the pinned imported corollary as its explicit mathematical supplier.
